item.title: A Directed Cubical Framework for k-critical Bipersistence Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.00261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In topological data analysis, multiparameter persistence modules (MPMs) are used to analyze data with multiple parameters. Summarizing topological information for MPMs is a non-trivial task; one useful summary of bipersistence modules is the fibered barcode \cite{lesnick2015interactive,lesnick2025fast}. In this paper, we use a directed topological construction of the parameter space of a bifiltration to extend the fibered barcode. Specifically, given a $k$-critical bifiltration $F$, we build an associated directed Euclidean cubical complex $C$ whose directed paths each correspond to a one-parameter subfiltration of $F$. The path space of $C$, $\di{C}$, is used to define the \emph{extended fibered barcode}, which contains all possible monotonically increasing paths in $C$. We show that there can be paths in $\di{C}$ which generate filtrations not obtainable along a line with positive slope, and that all lines with positive slope have a path in $\di{C}$ that generate an equivalent barcode. We introduce two types of equivalence for these restricted modules: combinatorial equivalence of diagrams, and simplicial equivalence of the filtrations generating the modules. We show that removing certain cubes from $C$ yields a subcomplex on which dihomotopic paths induce simplicially equivalent filtrations, and hence combinatorially equivalent diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Robin Belton, Robyn Brooks, Lisbeth Fajstrup, Brittany Terese Fasy, Elizabeth Vidaurre

item.title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.00799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance. Explicit graph filtrations illustrate the groupoid-valued construction, and so we suggest a new approach to interpret persistence diagrams and large data sets in topological data analysis, based on recent works of A-homotopy theory of the last years.
item.dc:creator: Yanga Bavuma, Martin Mijangos, Francesco G. Russo

item.title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.00825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations. The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.
item.dc:creator: Urtzi Buijs, Jos\'e Manuel Moreno Fern\'andez

item.title: A sphere-product counterexample to the additivity of homology nilpotency
item.description: arXiv:2611.01567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homology nilpotency need not increase under a product with a sphere. We construct a simply connected, closed smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $53$, rationally elliptic with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(\pi_*(M)\otimes\mathbb Q\bigr)=7$, such that $cat_0(M)=10$ and $Hnil(M\times S^2)=Hnil(M)=11$. The inequality $Hnil(X\times Y)\leq Hnil(X)+Hnil(Y)$ can therefore be strict even for a product of a closed manifold with $S^2$ as the second factor.
item.dc:creator: Paul-Eug\`ene Parent

item.title: Fixed points via tilting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we initiate the study of perfect commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in the non-connective setting. As an application we show that given a finite $C_p$-space $X$ the $\mathbb{F}_p$-cochains on $X^{C_p}$ can be recovered as a base-change of the tilt of the Tate construction on cochains on $X^e$.
item.dc:creator: Robert Burklund, Vignesh Subramanian

item.title: Unfolding of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.01994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Lurie's proposed description of left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories in terms of purely $\infty$-categorical data. More precisely, unfolding gives an equivalence between left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories and complete categorical chain complexes of rigid symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories. More generally, unfolding identifies skeletal sequences with categorical chain complexes without the completeness condition. We extend these equivalences to $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and, stably, obtain an equivalence between complete unbounded categorical chain complexes and left rigid categorical spectra. We also analyze their groupoid completion and express the homotopy groups of the associated spaces and spectra in terms of categorical cycles and boundaries. As examples, we construct the categorical chain complexes associated to geometric and algebraic bordism categories, including their equivariant variants, and to iterated span categories. Their localizations recover classical bordism and $L$-groups, while the span examples are related to algebraic $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Rune Haugseng, Thomas Nikolaus

item.title: Cohomology of regular spherical actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study regular spherical actions, namely, actions of a connected compact Lie group G on a manifold M with equidimensional orbits, some of which are spheres. These spherical orbits are diffeomorphic to homogeneous spaces G/H, and there is a list of nine possible families of pairs (G, H). The normalizer N of H in G plays an important role in our calculations, as does the Weyl group W = N/H. In fact, there are three possibilities for W, namely: Z_2, S^1 and S^3. The goal of this paper is to relate the cohomology of M to that of the orbit space M/G. We obtain a particularly simple relationship in the first case, W = Z_2. For the remaining two cases, W = S^1 and W = S^3, it is already known that the cohomology of M and that of the orbit space M/G are related by the Gysin sequence ... \to H^k(M/G) \to H^k(M ) \to H^{k-d}(M/G) \to H^{k+1}(M/G) \to ... In this work, we provide a direct construction of this sequence, avoiding the use of spectral sequences. Moreover, we give an explicit description of the connecting homomorphism as multiplication by a power of the Euler class associated with the action of the Weyl group W = S^l on the fixed-point set M^H.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ignacio Royo Prieto, Martintxo Saralegi-Aranguren, Robert Wolak

item.title: $S_n$-equivariant $L$-classes of Cartesian powers of Witt spaces and the Hodge index conjecture for symmetric products
item.description: arXiv:2611.02577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a compact oriented even-dimensional Witt pseudomanifold $X$, we compute the $S_n$-equivariant Banagl--Zagier $L$-classes of $X^n$ in terms of the Goresky--MacPherson $L$-classes of $X$ and the intersection cohomology Euler characteristic of $X$. This generalizes a theorem of Zagier for manifolds. Our approach is based on analyzing the equivariant structure of the signature operator of $X^n$ using equivariant $KK$-theory and power operations in analytic $K$-homology. We establish an analytic $K$-homology analogue of Moonen's algebraic localization theorem by proving that the localized Chern character of the $n$-th power operation, evaluated at an $n$-cycle, agrees with the $n$-th homological Adams operation applied to the Chern character. As an application, we prove that the characteristic class Hodge index conjecture for singular varieties, formulated by Brasselet--Sch\"urmann--Yokura, is preserved under taking symmetric products of complex projective varieties.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadali Aligholi

item.title: Indecomposable Uniform Families on the Adams 4-Line
item.description: arXiv:2611.02614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the $f_j$, $p_j$, $D_3(j)$, and $p_j'$ families on the 4-line of the classical Adams spectral sequence all conform to the Uniform Doomsday Conjecture. We do so by first using Bruner's formula to establish uniform families of differentials on these classes. We then study the Burklund-Xu and Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences to ensure that the differential targets are nonzero. The $f_j$ family requires further analysis of possible Adams $d_2$ differentials since the $f_j$ support uniform $d_3$ differentials. As a result of our work, only two indecomposable $\text{Sq}^0$ families remain to be settled in Adams filtration 4.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Benson, Runji Li

item.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.00813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Arora, Vivek Mohan Mallick

item.title: Du Bois cohomology of noncommutative spaces and the Hodge numbers invariance conjecture for singular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.01508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the definition of cdh-sheafified Hochschild homology from varieties to stable categories linear over a field of characteristic zero, thereby proving its Morita-invariance. The dimensions of its homology groups give meaningful numerical invariants of a category; we combine them with invariants coming from topological K-theory and Poincar\'e duality to prove equality of mixed Hodge numbers for singular complex projective Fourier--Mukai partners in several classes in dimensions two, three, and four, including normal surfaces and threefolds with rational singularities and equal irregularity. Beyond these applications, we construct Du Bois versions of topological cyclic homology of stable categories together with appropriate multiplicative structures, prove a Geller--Weibel-type result for the variants of negative cyclic homology we introduce, and give categorical characterizations of cohomological purity of proper varieties and the $\mathbb{Q}$-factoriality defect of complex projective threefolds with rational singularities.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Konovalov

item.title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.01916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.
item.dc:creator: Rune Haugseng

item.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
item.dc:creator: Baoyu Zhang, Shengmin Zhang

item.title: Motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces at the characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.02320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a novel, homotopy theoretic model for the motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces $K(Z_{(p)}(n), 2n) \in Spc(k)$ over fields of characteristic p. Using this, we determine their motives and, consequently, determine the motivic Steenrod algebra at the characteristic. Applications include the Hopkins--Morel isomorphism over arbitrary base schemes as well as the computation of the p-completed motivic stable stems and algebraic cobordism groups of fields of characteristic p. Along the way we expand the theory of normed algebraic structures in motivic homotopy theory, compare them to derived algebra at the characteristic, and produce a functor computing the motivic homology of the $P^1$-loop spaces of (certain) motivic spaces in terms of the motives.
item.dc:creator: Tom Bachmann, Michael J. Hopkins

item.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.03064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.
item.dc:creator: Grigorios Giotopoulos

item.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
item.description: arXiv:2611.03176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandra Kukie{\l}ka, Maksym Szemer, Szymon Buchaniec, Katarzyna Berent, Grzegorz Brus

item.title: Pontryagin-Weiss classes and a rational decomposition of spaces of homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2504.20265v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a rational homotopy pullback decomposition for variants of the classifying space of the group of homeomorphisms for a large class of manifolds. This has various applications, including a rational section of the stabilisation map ${\rm Top}(d)\rightarrow {\rm Top}$ of the space of homeomorphisms of ${\bf R}^d$ for $d\ge 6$, or a new method to construct topological bundles and detect characteristic classes thereof. Some steps in the proofs may be of independent interest, such as the construction of a nullhomotopy of the twice-iterated stabilisation map for the space of orientation-preserving derived automorphisms of the rational $E_d$-operad, results on recovering boundaries of manifolds from their interior in the context of embedding calculus, or a treatment of tensor products of truncated $\infty$-operads.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Krannich, Alexander Kupers

item.title: Constructions of contractibility in finite subset spaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.09815v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The space of all finite non-empty subsets of a topological space $X$, also known as the Ran space of $X$, is weakly contractible for $X$ path connected. We consider subspaces $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ of the Ran space given by all subsets of $X$ of size at most $n$, and their first homotopy groups. These groups are known to be trivial for $n\geqslant 3$, though the proofs are not constructive. We draw an explicit contraction in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 3}(S^1)$ of the generator of $\pi_1(S^1)$, which we then use to conclude that the induced maps $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 2n+1}(X))$ and $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n+2}(X))$ are trivial for all positive integers $n$. Pathological maps with infinitely many strata changes in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ are resolved via locally contractible neighbourhoods and exit paths. From this we conclude the triviality of $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X))$, for all $n\geqslant 3$.
item.dc:creator: J\=anis Lazovskis

item.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.26786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.
item.dc:creator: Henri Riihim\"aki, Jason P. Smith

item.title: Extending Goldberg's Exact Sequence to Braid Groups of Graphs and Simplicial Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2608.14350v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite connected simplicial complex $X$, the strand map $\iota_\ast$, from $\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ to $\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_1(X,x_i^0)$, sends a pure braid to the homotopy classes of its strands. A theorem of Goldberg (1973) computes its kernel when $X$ is a closed surface other than $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$: the kernel is the normal closure of the pure braids supported in an embedded disc. We extend this picture to arbitrary finite connected simplicial complexes. Call $X$ $\textit{weakly Goldberg}$ if some contractible subcomplex $X_0\subseteq X$ realises Goldberg's description, $\ker\iota_\ast=\left\langle \operatorname{im}(\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)) \right\rangle$, and $\textit{Goldberg}$ if $X_0$ can moreover be chosen so that $\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ is injective. We prove that the strand map is surjective if and only if $X\not\cong S^1$; that $X$ is weakly Goldberg if and only if its free part is a forest; and that $X$ is Goldberg if and only if it admits an $\textit{admissible tree}$ -- a maximal tree of a scaffold, compatible with the boundary and interior types of the attachments of the free part to the thick components. We also classify the complexes for which the kernel is trivial, settle the exceptional surfaces $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$, and obtain complete answers for manifolds and for graphs. The main tools are a graph-of-spaces decomposition of the configuration space at a point of $X$ and a resolution procedure reducing an arbitrary complex to a simple model.
item.dc:creator: Byung Hee An

item.title: Interval Replacements of Persistence Modules
item.description: arXiv:2403.08308v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Persistence modules indexed by finite posets arise in topological data analysis. Unlike in the one-parameter case, they need not decompose into interval modules. Interval replacements approximate them by formal differences of interval decomposable modules. Extending earlier work on 2D-grids, we study these replacements for arbitrary compression systems. Different choices can give different interval rank invariants and replacements, including those related to interval resolutions on commutative ladders. Our main results are an explicit formula for interval ranks and an essential-cover theorem. Using Auslander--Reiten theory, we express interval ranks in terms of ranks of matrices formed from the structure maps of the module. The essential-cover theorem recovers each interval rank from a suitable restriction of the module. The replacement construction preserves the corresponding interval rank invariant, which recovers the usual rank invariant on segments. Essential covers also give a sufficient condition for two compression systems to yield the same invariant. For total compression, the invariant coincides with the generalized rank invariant of Kim and M\'emoli. On 2D-grids, essential covers recover the zigzag formula of Dey, Kim, and M\'emoli for this invariant.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba (Department of Mathematics, Shizuoka University, Osaka Central Advanced Mathematical Institute, Osaka Metropolitan University), Etienne Gauthier (\'Ecole Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris), Enhao Liu (Institute for Advanced Study, Kyoto University)
